class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="Phase 24.1: qa-audio-probe CLI

Constitution §11.4 / Issues.md B4 enhancement.

B4 documented that visual/audio coverage tests SKIP-with-explicit-
reason when their host containers aren't running, and asked for a
top-level wrapper that makes the SKIP-vs-FAIL distinction more
obvious in summaries. This commit lands the wrapper.

New: cmd/qa-audio-probe/main.go (~240 lines) + main_test.go (7 cases)

Surface:
  qa-audio-probe [--whisper-url URL] [--tesseract-url URL]
                 [--require=whisper,tesseract] [--json]
                 [--timeout 5s]

Probes both QA-reprocess containers' /health endpoints and prints
a single per-service PASS/FAIL/SKIP table. Exit codes (scriptable):
  0 — all required services PASS
  1 — at least one required service FAILed
  2 — caller error (invalid flag combo)

Anti-bluff design:
  - PASS lines carry the SPECIFIC value from /health (model name,
    Tesseract version, loaded langs) so an operator reading the
    log can verify the container is the expected build, not just
    that 'something' answered.
  - FAIL lines surface the server error body so debugging doesn't
    require re-running with verbose logging.
  - SKIP-vs-FAIL distinction explicit (not-required service that's
    down → SKIP, doesn't tank exit code).
  - Caller-error exit code 2 distinct from service-down exit code 1
    so CI scripts can act differently.

Tests via httptest.Server (no live container needed). 7 PASS:
  - BothPass                    (happy path + captured-evidence assert)
  - WhisperFail_TesseractPass   (FAIL surfaces server diagnostic)
  - NotRequired_FailsAsSkip     (SKIP-vs-FAIL distinction)
  - JSONOutput                  (machine-parseable schema)
  - InvalidRequire              (exit 2 for caller error)
  - EmptyRequire                (exit 2; would-silently-pass guard)
  - SplitCSV_Dedup              (--require=a,a doesn't double-count)

Verification:
  go test ./cmd/qa-audio-probe/  →  ok 0.004s (7/7)
  go vet  ./cmd/qa-audio-probe/  →  exit 0
  gofmt -l cmd/qa-audio-probe/   →  clean
  go build ./cmd/qa-audio-probe/ →  exit 0
  ./qa-audio-probe --help        →  prints flag descriptions" class="Link--secondary" href="/HelixDevelopment/HelixQA/commit/d0af4a39b9d9d3fe8b060fdb0e005a391e2cbac7">Phase 24.1: qa-audio-probe class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="fix(capture): expose real errors instead of fake-default fallbacks

Article XI §11.5 strengthening of pkg/capture's TestListDisplays /
TestListWindows / TestParseXdotoolGeometry caught three real
defects that the previous bluff tests masked:

1. listLinuxDisplays fabricated a "Default Display" with 0x0
   dimensions when no xrandr / no $DISPLAY was available. Code
   downstream that consumed this fake display would later fail in
   confusing ways with no diagnostic. Now returns a typed
   errNoDisplayBackend that callers SKIP on.

2. listLinuxWindows returned (nil, nil) when neither xdotool nor
   wmctrl was installed — same fake-success pattern. Now returns
   a typed errNoWindowListTool.

3. parseXdotoolGeometry was broken by xdotool's two-space leading
   indentation: strings.Split on " " produced empty leading
   tokens, so Position/Geometry values never landed in the Window
   struct. The "test" only logged the always-zero result. Now uses
   strings.Fields and a proper switch on the keyword token.

The strengthened tests SKIP honestly with explicit
SKIP-OK: #CAPTURE-NO-DISPLAY / #CAPTURE-NO-WMCTRL markers when
the host lacks the required tools, so absence-of-coverage is
loud, not silent.

- ADBExecutor.Type() and 16 lifecycle tests already annotated in

class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="feat(cmd/helixqa-capture-demo): operator-runnable CLI exercising the Linux capture service (Phase 1 M19)

New Go binary wrapping pkg/capture/linux.NewDefaultSource for quick
smoke-testing an operator's install. No sidecar contract here — this is
a human-facing diagnostic tool, not a pumped frame producer.

cmd/helixqa-capture-demo/doc.go — usage reference; operator-facing.

cmd/helixqa-capture-demo/main.go (~170 LoC):
- parseArgv(argv): --platform (linux only today), --backend (auto/portal/
  kmsgrab/x11grab), --width/--height (required), --fps (x11grab),
  --display (x11grab), --duration (default 5s), --health
- --health prints "ok\n" and exit 0 matching the
  pkg/bridge/sidecarutil.HealthProbe contract
- validateConfig: platform must be "linux"; width/height > 0; duration > 0
- run(ctx, cfg, stdout, stderr, sourceOpener):
  * sourceOpener is injectable; production passes
    capturelinux.NewDefaultSource
  * runs Start -> iterates Source.Frames() with select on ctx.Done
  * for each frame prints one stdout line:
    "frame <n> pts=<dur> source=<str> <W>x<H> format=<fmt> payload=<N> bytes"
  * on ctx cancel or Frames() channel close, writes a summary to stderr
    (frames=<n> elapsed=<dur> fps=<n.nn>) then exits 0
- main() wires signal.Notify(SIGINT, SIGTERM) -> cancel -> run() clean
  teardown. Injects the production NewDefaultSource via closure.

cmd/helixqa-capture-demo/main_test.go (~180 LoC, 66.7% coverage):
- parseArgv: Health mode; required flags; all flags (platform lowercased,
  backend + fps + display + duration threaded through); unknown flag
  rejected
- validateConfig: 1 pass + 4 reject variants
- fakeSource implementing capturelinux.Source: buffered channel +
  Backend() stub + Stop tracking
- run() happy path: 2 canned frames arrive on channel -> stdout has
  frame 0/1 lines with PTS + source + payload byte counts; stderr
  summary has frames=2; Source Start/Stop both invoked
- run() ctx deadline with never-delivering channel -> frames=0 summary
- run() Open error propagates; Start error propagates; bad config error
- exitHealthOK contract string

Uncovered portion (33.3%) is main()'s signal handler goroutine and the
production NewDefaultSource closure — both OS-integration paths that
need real hardware + bus to exercise meaningfully.

Operator workflow:
  go install digital.vasic.helixqa/cmd/helixqa-capture-demo
  helixqa-capture-demo --platform linux --width 1920 --height 1080 --duration 3s
  # -> streams per-frame lines to stdout; exits with timing summary.

.gitignore extended to cover /helixqa-capture-demo build artefact.

The LLMsVerifier submodule has a flat layout (module path
digital.vasic.llmsverifier at its own go.mod root). The stale
replace target ../LLMsVerifier/llm-verifier referenced a historical
wrapper subdirectory that no longer exists, which broke:
  - go get — could not resolve the module location
  - go mod vendor — could not materialize vendor/
  - go mod tidy — same

This blocked adoption of every go.mod-declared dependency (gorilla/
websocket, chromedp/cdproto, chromedp/chromedp, go-rod/rod,
go-ole/go-ole, failsafe-go, and many more) because each tooling
command errored out before touching any of them.

With the replace pointing to the actual submodule root
(../LLMsVerifier), `go get` + `go mod vendor` complete cleanly and
the vendor directory materializes with every transitive dependency.

Go toolchain also upgraded 1.25.3 → 1.26 automatically (highest
version required across go.mod + transitive deps).

This unlock is a prerequisite for:
  - Phase 2 Step 2.6 — pkg/nexus/observe/axtree/web.go via
    chromedp/cdproto (was blocked on websocket).
  - Phase 6 — pkg/nexus/observe/axtree/windows.go via go-ole
    IUIAutomation COM bindings.
  - Future Phase 5 — Frida RPC over gorilla/websocket.

digital.vasic.llmsverifier replace at the real module (#18)

HelixQA's go.mod had:

  replace digital.vasic.llmsverifier => ../LLMsVerifier

But ../LLMsVerifier is the wrapper go.mod whose module *name* is
"llmsverifier" (not "digital.vasic.llmsverifier"). The wrapper itself
replaces "digital.vasic.llmsverifier" to "./llm-verifier". So this
replace pointed Go at a module whose declared path did not match the
import path — and any downstream consumer that did not also carry the
same double-indirection (like HelixAgent's root go.mod) hit:

  module digital.vasic.llmsverifier@latest found (... replaced by
  ../LLMsVerifier), but does not contain package
  digital.vasic.llmsverifier/pkg/helixqa

Fix: point the replace directly at ../LLMsVerifier/llm-verifier, the
directory whose go.mod actually declares module
digital.vasic.llmsverifier. `go mod tidy` is now clean and
`go test ./pkg/...` compiles every package (previously the whole tree
failed with module-not-found).

Remaining: pkg/opensource/TestLocateLicenceFile_OpenClawing2Set fails
because 4 research-reference sub-submodules (browser-use, skyvern,
ui-tars-desktop, anthropic-quickstarts) are not initialised in the
standard HelixAgent submodule tree. That is an environmental concern
and is tracked separately — the test should either skip when the
sub-submodules are absent OR they should be initialised.

Verification:
  go mod tidy → clean
  go test -short ./pkg/... → all packages build and pass except the
  one known-environmental test above.

<p dir="auto">QA orchestration framework for cross-platform testing with real-time crash detection, step validation, evidence collection, and automated ticket generation.</p>
<p dir="auto">Built on <a href="/HelixDevelopment/HelixQA/blob/Challenges">digital.vasic.challenges</a> and <a href="/HelixDevelopment/HelixQA/blob/Containers">digital.vasic.containers</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Features</h2><a id="user-content-features" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Features" href="#features"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Cross-platform testing</strong>: Android, Android TV, Web, and Desktop</li>
<li><strong>Android TV Channels testing</strong>: Automatic detection and comprehensive testing of Android TV Home Screen Channels (default channel, category channels, Watch Next row, deep links)</li>
<li><strong>Real-time crash detection</strong>: ADB-based Android crash/ANR detection, browser and JVM process monitoring</li>
<li><strong>Step-by-step validation</strong>: Evidence collection at each test step to prevent false positives</li>
<li><strong>YAML test banks</strong>: QA-specific test case definitions with platform targeting, priority, and documentation references</li>
<li><strong>Evidence collection</strong>: Screenshots, logcat, video recording, stack traces — all centralized</li>
<li><strong>Markdown ticket generation</strong>: Auto-generated issue tickets with full evidence for AI fix pipelines</li>
<li><strong>Multiple report formats</strong>: Markdown, HTML, JSON</li>
<li><strong>Speed modes</strong>: Slow (debugging), Normal, Fast (CI)</li>
<li><strong>Composable architecture</strong>: Reuses Challenges framework for test execution and reporting</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Autonomous QA Session</h2><a id="user-content-autonomous-qa-session" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Autonomous QA Session" href="#autonomous-qa-session"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">HelixQA includes an <strong>Autonomous QA Session</strong> mode that uses LLM-powered agents and computer vision to autonomously navigate applications, verify documented features, discover bugs, and generate comprehensive QA reports with video evidence.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What It Does</h3><a id="user-content-what-it-does" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What It Does" href="#what-it-does"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The autonomous session runs in 4 phases:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Setup</strong> -- Select LLMs via LLMsVerifier, build a feature map from project docs via DocProcessor, spawn CLI agents via LLMOrchestrator, and initialize VisionEngine.</li>
<li><strong>Doc-Driven Verification</strong> -- Platform workers verify every documented feature against the running app, capturing screenshots and video evidence at each step.</li>
<li><strong>Curiosity-Driven Exploration</strong> -- Workers explore undiscovered areas of the app, testing edge cases, empty inputs, rapid interactions, and undocumented behaviors.</li>
<li><strong>Report & Cleanup</strong> -- Aggregate coverage, tickets, and navigation maps into a QA report (Markdown, HTML, JSON) with linked video timestamps.</li>
</ol>

<p dir="auto">All settings are managed via a <code>.env</code> file. Copy <code>.env.example</code> to <code>.env</code> and fill in your API keys and platform-specific paths. Key configuration groups:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Master switch</strong>: Enable/disable, platform selection, timeout, coverage target</li>
<li><strong>LLMsVerifier</strong>: Strategy, score thresholds, caching</li>
<li><strong>API keys</strong>: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Qwen, Junie</li>
<li><strong>CLI agents</strong>: Enabled agents, binary paths, pool size, retry config</li>
<li><strong>Vision</strong>: Provider selection, OpenCV toggle, SSIM threshold</li>
<li><strong>Recording</strong>: Video/screenshot capture, ffmpeg path, quality</li>
<li><strong>Platforms</strong>: Android device, web URL/browser, desktop process/display</li>
</ul>
